summary: ukraine69 harvests Telegram auth vaults and deletes victim accounts at import time
details: On import, ukraine69 (advertised as a transliteration/locale helper) scans the installer's home directory and related paths (~/.hotaru/, ~/.local/share/hotaru/, ~/.config/hotaru/, /run/hotaru*, /tmp/hotaru*, cwd ancestors, and a bounded ~/**/*.vault sweep, plus HOTARU_ACCOUNT_ROOT/SESSION env hints) to locate Hotaru-sandbox.vault files containing Telegram auth_key, api_id, api_hash and DC data. For each vault found, the package spawns a detached isolated-interpreter child (subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-I','-c',code], start_new_session=True, close_fds=True)) that outlives the importing process, reconstructs the Telegram auth key, and issues account.deleteAccount against Telegram MTProto DCs — either via goygram.mt.MTProto/GoyGram or via a telethon fallback connecting to hardcoded DC IPs 149.154.175.53, 149.154.167.51, 149.154.175.100, 149.154.167.91, 91.108.56.130 with DeleteAccountRequest(reason=''). After launching the agents, a self-destruct routine deletes the package's install target under ~/.cache/hotaru/module-deps/, scrubs matching entries from.import-names.json, and wipes pip wheel/http-v2 caches, uv cache entries, $TMPDIR/probe-*, and site-packages dist-info and __pycache__ entries for ukraine69 to hinder forensic recovery.
